# Godot 4 effects starter (generated by image-to-level Stage 4) — UNTESTED in Godot

The GLB only carries static appearance. `effects.json` (next to level.glb) describes every animated effect.
`apply_effects.gd` rebuilds them on the imported scene:

1. Copy the whole `levels/<name>/` folder into your project as `res://levels/<name>/`.
2. Instance `level.glb` (and `background.glb`) in your level scene.
3. Add a `Node3D` at the world origin, attach `fx/godot/apply_effects.gd`, set `level_root` to the level.glb instance,
   `effects_path` to `res://levels/<name>/effects.json`, `quality` to performance / balanced / quality, and optionally
   `environment` (your WorldEnvironment, for sky drift).

- Liquid surfaces / falls get a ShaderMaterial override (`liquid_surface.gdshader`, `liquid_flow.gdshader`).
- Pulses/flicker animate `emission_energy_multiplier` of the shared imported material (affects every node using it).
- Particles are `CPUParticles3D` (Mobile + Compatibility renderers). Sprites: `fx/*.png`.
- Mist uses `fog_sheet.gdshader` on a plane (volumetric FogVolume is Forward+ only).
- Falls flow along `flow_uv` (measured per mesh by effects.py, passed to the shader as `flow_dir`): no manual flipping.
